caption:
The FCC just rewrote the rules on text opt-outs.

Right now, one STOP reply to any automated text, whether it's a reminder, a review request, or a missed-call text-back, can cancel every text you're allowed to send that person.

On September 30, the FCC adopted order 26-67. Once it takes effect, a STOP on an informational text like an appointment reminder only cancels that category. A STOP on a marketing text still cancels all marketing.

It isn't law yet. The rule starts 30 days after the FCC publishes it in the Federal Register, no exact date set.

Get ahead of it this week:

1. Sort your automated texts into two buckets: informational (reminders, confirmations, missed-call replies) and marketing (promos, review asks)

2. Pick one opt-out word and put it on every template in both buckets

The Follow-Up Builder helps you build and tag sequences the right way.
